shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a fixed 146,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine, with snow, altitude weather and windier peaks. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched.
body:
# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~67 files, ~18,100 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY. Generation cost (§9) has had its first real diagnosis and its first big fix; the headline A/B is still outstanding.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)*64`; **64-alignment is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position, so a non-multiple offset makes the ground "randomise" between a level and its see-below view). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map. First suspect for any "smeared or stretched" symptom.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
The surface band is a horizontal SLICE of a tall map, so anything vanilla anchors to the map's extent lands in the wrong band.

| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims | water surface (§6b-LAKE) | none, cosmetic, accepted |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16) | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Map-wide scalar is the nastiest: the value is correct, just not per-band, so nothing looks wrong in the code. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 146,000 cells, FIXED
`4 x 190 = 145,920` sets the figure. `5 x 190` and `3 x 254` are refused. `ABMapSizeLimit` owns it.
Per-level size is SQUARE (`Size.x == bandHeight`), which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (it squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, which is the vanilla control for "is this even our bug". Band count sets `Size.z`, so the chooser is a calibrated aspect dial: 1 band = 1.00, 2 = 2.02, 4 = 4.04.
**⚠ STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?** Pre-flight check: the strip must read 1 level and 36,100 cells.

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play; the postfix also re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` every frame, undoing every click. Now our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix, because vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height.
**The level spinners are NOT known to be broken.** Run #190 produced a `3 up / 0 down` map when `0 up / 3 down` was intended, and that was USER ERROR, confirmed by the user. Do not re-open this without new evidence. The settings persist between colonies, so an unchanged chooser silently reuses the last plan; that is the likeliest explanation for any "wrong plan" report.

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong. **Multi-hop routing is STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY** (needs a stair tower).

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
Three wrong layers before the right one. Correct answer: `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof, because only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix is to normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. NINE systems share it. **Seven separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug**; grep every `- Slot` before trusting new code.
Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts are on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level. Now independently confirmed by timing: see §9's sign flip.
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position. Printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields nothing at all.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` mirrors the internal Watergen and overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately) preserving the roll. `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators still streaked. No flow data exists in the process, so flow cannot be the cause. **The ghost-river theory is dead; do not revive it.** Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, so a river cell outside every sample radius writes NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c, 6d, 6e. COMPAT AND COASTS (all verified)
**Dubs Mint Minimap:** ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only, no foreign type in any patch-class signature.
**Map Preview:** it never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`, and a slice of position-based noise is a different map. Fix is to generate at full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896).
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. Fix is `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`, with NO SCALING. Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, both applied AFTER the settings clamp.

**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** `SteadyEnvironmentEffectsTick` computes `outdoorMeltAmount` once per tick for the whole map and never calls `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. The line was dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.

**Climate defaults** (now per colony, §17): +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. **No ceiling clamp by design.**

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `maxZoom` left DERIVED. `panMargin` 63.5 now applies to EVERY level. `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED.

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST: FIRST REAL DIAGNOSIS (runs #188, #190)

## 9a. The profile now stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints a `TILE` line (tile id, biome, hilliness, elevation, temp, rainfall, coastal, mutators) and a `PLAN` line (bands, band height, surface band, up/down split, doomed cell count). **Added because four earlier carve timings were recorded without the tile and are therefore uninterpretable.** It caught a confound on its very first use: an intended repeat landed on a different tile and the timings had to be discarded.
It also prints two censuses, `DESTROYED by def` and `SUPPRESSED by def`, plus a `SCOPING:` line stamping the state of every scoping toggle (§12's stale-toggle rule).

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION
Run #188, tile 846, TemperateForest / Mountainous / Mountain+Caves, 190x768, 4 bands:

| Phase | ms |
|---|---|
| All 42 gensteps combined (wall) | 3,972 |
| AB band carve | **20,447** |
| of which `Sky clear` bands 1-3 | **20,126** (98.4% of carve) |
| `Map.FinalizeInit` | 169 |
| things destroyed | 74,584 |

Generation is 16% of the cost, destruction 84%. **The earlier framing that scoping saves "both halves" was WRONG.** Even a perfect skip of every genstep could only ever save ~4 s, much of it legitimate surface work. The prize is the 20.1 s of deletion.
Per-destroy price is ~0.19 to 0.27 ms and is STABLE across three runs on three tiles. Only the op COUNT ever moves, so **op count is the only lever**. The price is the engine's: `ListerThings` removal is a linear `List.Remove` over lists holding ~100k things, which is why the saving is superlinear.

**Corollary, settled:** carving before `FinalizeInit` to avoid a double region build is worth at most 169 ms of 24,600. That line of inquiry is CLOSED.

## 9c. The culprit was rock, and that is now a fact
74,584 destroys over 108,300 doomed cells is 0.689 per cell. `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` walks `map.AllCells` and spawns rock wherever elevation > 0.7 outside a cave.
Proven by census, not inference (run #190, tile 97261, Desert / Mountainous / Mountain):
- `SUPPRESSED` 43,517 rock (Granite 26,789 + Limestone 16,728)
- `DESTROYED` 4,939 total, of which rock is 238
Rock moved out of the destroy column into the suppressed column, 99.5% of it. Would-be total 48,456, so **rock was 90% of everything the carve deleted**.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses the `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` call inside `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` when the target cell is in a doomed SKY band. Three properties make it safe:
- **Shape.** Per-cell noise test, no fixed count being redistributed. Same licence as the plant skip. This is the line dividing safe from unsafe scoping.
- **State-neutrality.** Only the SPAWN is suppressed; roofs, the small-group roof cleanup and `ScatterLumpsMineable` all still run. `ClearCellHard` never touched roofs, so `ABSkyBandGen` receives bit-identical state.
- **Sky bands only.** `FillRock` KEEPS vanilla rock where the def matches its vein noise, so suppressing in the basement swaps a free keep for a fresh spawn. This is a SEMANTIC split (sky erases, basement consumes), NOT the per-band cost heuristic that #174/#175 falsified.
Patched on the `ThingDef` overload rather than the `Thing` funnel, so the cancel happens before `ThingMaker.MakeThing`.

## 9e. Facts and open items
**⚠ FALSIFIED, still dead: "band 1 is consistently ~3x bands 2-3."** Per-band cost is a property of where that tile's noise put rock.
**Sign flip, and it is a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` per band INVERTED, 125 / 415 / 528 rising with altitude where run #188 read 7517 / 7029 / 5580 falling. Rock tapers upward (§6), so higher bands have more OPEN ground and chunks/rubble only grow on open ground. Same fact from the other side.
**Biome content drives cost, not cell count:** 7.4x spread at identical size and band count. Any carve timing MUST record the tile.
**Precedent:** `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands` took 16.9 s to 4.2 s.
**Do not blanket-skip** the water or coast mutators; §6b, §6e and §6d depend on them running correctly anchored.

## 9f. Next targets, ranked by the census
1. **`GenStep_RockChunks`**, 88% of what survives: `Filth_RubbleRock` 3,183 + `ChunkGranite` 598 + `ChunkLimestone` 585 = 4,366 of 4,939. Verified per-cell probabilistic (`PlaceProbabilityPerCell`, then `GrowLowRockFormationFrom`), so it passes the shape test. Worth roughly 0.9 s.
2. **Scattered ruins, which are also a CONTENT BUG.** `73 Wall`, `15 AncientFence`, `12 AncientGiantWheel`, `148 Filth_MachineBits`, `13 Steel` were deleted from doomed bands. Per §2 a scatterer's count is already sized for ONE band, but its placement spans the whole stack, so **the surface band is losing a large share of the ruins vanilla intended**. Scoping fixes content and cost together. ⚠ Paired risk: run #190 logged `Scatterer GenStep_ScatterLayout from def AncientExostriderRemains could not find cell to generate at`, the §15b starvation signal, so the derived seam margin must be re-checked at the same time.

# 10, 11. PERF AND LINKS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns, mod approximately 2% of frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry. Elevator SHIPPED but untested; full-mesh 2x2, O(n^2) in band count.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
Band info, below layer and pawn reports, water report, transit health, stuck probe, lighting/shader/biome reports, bisect toggles, ABGenProfile (now tile-stamped and census-bearing), camera calibration.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** Run #172 opened with `belowWater=False` left from an earlier session, which mimics a fixed bug exactly. Every scoping toggle is now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE for this reason.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.** Single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered out of the summaries. Confirmed again in #190: the scatterer starvation warning and a `DropThingsNear` failure both surfaced only via `monitor_poll`.
**⚠ The auto-prompt is edge-triggered per run.** A second occurrence of the same log call site never re-prompts, so a repeat measurement in the same session must be fetched with `monitor_get_error` (which returns the LATEST occurrence) or spotted via the `×count`.
`AB2: band info` is the fastest ground truth for "what did this map actually generate as"; it settled a level-plan question in one line.
The start-spot failure log is a first-class diagnostic; its cell census identified the coastline bug in one line.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **The headline A/B is still missing.** Repeat tile 846, `3 up / 0 down` at 190, with `skipRockInSkyBands=True`, against run #188's 20,447 ms carve / 74,584 destroys. Every other comparison so far has changed tile at the same time.
2. **⚠ A banded generation produced NO profile at all.** The 126x512 map in run #190 generated as banded (`AB2: band info` confirms 4 bands) yet `ABGenProfile.Report` never emitted, while the same call site had fired once earlier in the run. `Report` is unconditional in the `GenerateMap` postfix and no `band carve failed` error appeared. Unexplained; reproduce before trusting any single-run measurement.
3. **Unexplained in #190:** `DropThingsNear failed to find a place to drop Lai near (59, 0, 476)` on a map whose start spot was `(63, 0, 63)`. z=476 is three bands away. Possibly benign (that map's surface generated as solid rock, so the drop finder had nowhere to go and wandered), but not established.
4. §9f items 1 and 2.
5. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators**: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
6. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix. **Basement paths remain untested**; `surfaceBand>0` and band-folded addressing have still never run, and the one attempt in #190 was a mis-set plan.
7. Realtime-things pass still single-band. Selection bracket drifts upward as you zoom out. Waterfalls, combat never verified, vertical conduit, compat audit, **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound that invalidated it. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. Use the product's own knobs as lab equipment. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Not every bug has a bug. The absence of a known error line is a valid pass signal.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.** The whole doomed-band effort was framed as "stop generating waste"; generation turned out to be 16% and deletion 84%. The fix was right, the reason was wrong, and only the profile said so.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.** "74,584 things" is not a diagnosis; "43,517 Granite and Limestone" is. Attributing a bulk number to defs converted a plausible inference into a fact and simultaneously ranked the next three targets. Pair a SUPPRESSED census with a DESTROYED one so the two are a conservation check rather than one number taken on trust.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into the experiment's own output.** The tile stamp caught a changed tile on its first run and voided a comparison that would otherwise have been believed.
**⚠ Evidence that is consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence.** "The size selection stuck, so the level spinners must be broken" was wrong: an unchanged spinner reusing a persisted value produces exactly the same observation. Ask what a datum would look like under the OTHER hypothesis before spending it.
**⚠ Persisted settings are a silent confound.** The level plan survives between colonies, so a chooser left untouched reproduces the last run's layout and looks like a fresh choice.
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim, not a fact (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on. Verify a patched branch is even reachable before debugging your own logic.
**Shapes.** Classify into one of the six. A slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even symptom is arithmetic. When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Patch the idempotent READ, not the cached WRITE. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature. Read the foreign mod's OWN compat classes first. **Suppress the callee, not the caller**, when a genstep does several jobs and only one is waste; it keeps the change provably state-neutral.
**Engine facts.** `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Altitude is draw order, and `WorldClipper` sorts above `Skyfaller`. A null global texture falls back to the shader's default. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation, so generation-time patches must read the pending layout. Snapshot generated-world parameters onto the map. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. Never cache comps while Scribe is active. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. A `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole atlas sheet. Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED, which is why the same work costs ~40x after `FinalizeInit`.

---

# 15. QOL PASS (verified, run #172)
**15a. Nothing may exist in the void.** `ABBandSafety.cs`. Three redundant layers: the finders answer inside the surface band; a prefix on the 7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn` rewrites `loc` before vanilla reads it; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves. Always relocates to the SURFACE. Scoped to pawns and to the gutter only.
**15b. Structures must not straddle a seam.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases the distance onto the cell's own band rect and eleven cold call sites inherit it. Backstop: a postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt`. The seam margin is DERIVED (`bandHeight/24`, clamped 4 to 12); a flat 10 starved scatterers on small bands.
**15c. Camera bounds:** `panMargin` 63.5 on every level.
**15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge REMOVED on banded maps.** `ABNoBuildEdge.cs`. Per-band is one flag away. Stated consequence: vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge.
**15e. Drop pods fall through the levels.** `ABSkyfallerRelay.cs`. Suppress `Skyfaller.DrawAt` and re-issue once via `DrawNowAt`, translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Altitude chosen PER FRAME. `Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` excluded.

# 16. ALTITUDE AND WEATHER (`ABBandWeather.cs`, verified)
One weather INTERPRETED per band, since `WeatherManager` is per-Map.
- **Snow confined to real ground:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`.
- **Melt per band:** prefix on `DoCellSteadyEffects` rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call including level 0.
- **Snow must exist before it can persist:** `SeedAltitudeSnow` at generation, seeded from CURRENT temperature. Costs ~18 ms, free.
- **Rain falls and draws as snow above the line.** Accumulation via the public `AddFallenSnowAt`; vanilla gates on the cached field but takes the amount from the live property. Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def shared across maps.
- **No overlays underground**, judged on the viewed band.
- **Wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50, zero underground.** Patched on the `DesiredPowerOutput` getter. `CalculateWindCells` spans 22 rows and the gutter is 2.
- **Readout:** `GlobalControls.TemperatureString` rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. `MapTemperature.OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached by it, because outdoor cells still belong to a Room and `Room.Temperature` is a stored field.

# 17. SETTINGS PASS (verified)
**Tabbed and scrolling window:** Performance, Climate, Sky, Basement, Diagnostics. Tab row is hand-drawn buttons, not `TabDrawer`. Each tab draws inside a try/catch that renders the exception into the pane.

**⚠ The blank-tab bug.** Scroll-view content height is measured from the previous frame's `list.CurHeight`. Without a floor this is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH. Fix: `viewHeights[i] = Mathf.Max(list.CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`. Diagnosed by one label drawn OUTSIDE the scroll view.
**⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.** A fallback error message rendered inside a clipped region is silent, and its silence is not evidence.

**The unlock gate.** The checkbox writes to a LOCAL; `unclampMapSize` only becomes true inside the confirmation callback, so the stored value IS the record that the warning was read. While unlocked, a red banner reports the multiple over budget, coloured against the BUDGET, not against `Fits()`.
**The budget stays a `const`**, deliberately.
**Climate is SNAPSHOTTED onto `ABBandMap` at generation** (`SnapshotClimate`, scribed, called beside `Setup` on BOTH carve paths). Resolution order is snapshot, then settings, then hardcoded defaults.
Always shows 3 up and 3 down regardless of the current plan. Presets Gentle, Standard, Alpine.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`, `quicktest=false` (the level chooser needs the menus; Map Preview doubly so).
Compat tests need the target mod as a companion. Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) and Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) are both INACTIVE in the user's real list.
Water tests need a river or lake tile, coastline tests a coastal one. **Record the tile in any perf comparison; the profile now does this automatically, so read the TILE line before comparing two runs.**
**Re-check the level strip before generating.** The plan persists between colonies and an untouched chooser silently reuses it.
Read the bisect line before trusting any water or snow observation.
